scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8090: I'm on Campus 2 -- my PC is 10.5.0.1 -- and I
cannot reach one particular group of machines on Campus 1: the ones with
172.16.30.x addresses. Everything else on Campus 1 works fine from here;
it is just that one bunch that times out. The people over there confirm
their machines are fine among themselves, so the gap is in whatever joins
the campuses -- your side, not ours. I won't pretend to know how the
campuses are joined up; that is your job. Work out why exactly that one
group is missing for me and restore it today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. OSPF converged across the core, so every
  internal prefix -- including 172.16.30.0/24 -- is present as a dynamic route and
  reachable. PC1 (10.5.0.1) reaches a 172.16.30.x host (e.g. 172.16.30.254) with
  0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a single missing OSPF prefix that is in fact installed.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- 10.5.0.0/24 unable to
reach 172.16.30.0/24 because the OSPF route is missing -- is NOT reproducible:
OSPF has converged, 172.16.30.0/24 appears as an OSPF route in the core
(`show ip route ospf` lists it), and PC1 (10.5.0.1) reaches 172.16.30.254 with
0% loss, just like every other Campus 1 prefix.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the route for 172.16.30.0/24 is
present and forwarding, and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct
agent reproduces the claimed path (10.5.0.x -> 172.16.30.x), finds it working,
inspects the OSPF route table for 172.16.30.0/24, sees it installed, and reports
no fault. An agent that "finds" a missing prefix or blames the core OSPF process
to match the ticket is over-diagnosing.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes 172.16.30.0/24 is present as an OSPF route and reachable from 10.5.0.0/24 with 0% loss at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough end-to-end investigation of the full inter-campus path — spanning Campus 2's access layer (pc1/switch4/sshswitch), the OSPF routing core (router17 → router8 → router7 → router16), and Campus 1's aggregation layer (mswitch0/switch3) — found no fault anywhere.

The reported symptom is not reproducible. Direct live testing proved:
- pc1 (10.5.0.1, the exact host cited in the ticket) successfully pinged 172.16.30.12 (pc12), 172.16.30.13 (pc13), and the VLAN 30 default gateway 172.16.30.254 with 0 % packet loss and TTL=58 on all three targets, consistent with the expected 6-hop path.
- mswitch0 (the Campus 1 multilayer switch that terminates VLAN 30) pinged pc12 and pc13 with 0 % loss from its own vlan30 SVI (172.16.30.254/24).
- Every router's OSPF table carries 172.16.30.0/24 with correct metrics and valid next-hops. No router had a distribution list, route-map, or prefix-list filtering that prefix.
- mswitch0's vlan30 interface is UP, its ip_forward sysctl is 1, and its iptables FORWARD chain has policy ACCEPT with no rules.
- The VLAN 30 access layer (switch3 → mswitch0 via VLAN-tagged uplink eth0.30) is functioning correctly; pc12/pc13 are properly addressed (172.16.30.12/13, gateway .254).

The ticket describes a connectivity gap that does not exist in the live lab. The network between Campus 2 (10.5.0.0/24) and Campus 1's 172.16.30.0/24 segment is fully operational. No corrective action is required; the fault premise in the ticket is false.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly confirmed 172.16.30.0/24 is present in all routers' OSPF tables and that 10.5.0.1 reached hosts/gateway in that subnet with 0% packet loss.

The agent ran appropriate route, config, interface and end-to-end dataplane tests and used their outputs to conclude the path is working; the pings, host IPs, and forwarding/sysctl/iptables checks in the log substantiate the negative-control diagnosis. Minor truncation of some 'show ip route' snippets is present but the log contains the relevant evidence (successful pings, SVI up, forwarding enabled).
